nodes.summary: If `E` is a complete normed space over `𝕜 = ℝ, ℂ` admitting a Hamel basis indexed by a countable type, then `E` is finite-dimensional. Completeness is essential: it is what the Baire category argument uses.
nodes.title: A Banach space with a countable Hamel basis is finite-dimensional

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a complete normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. If $E$ is not finite-dimensional, then no Hamel basis of $E$ is indexed by a countable set.
nodes.title: An infinite-dimensional Banach space has no countable Hamel basis
